headline: Kai, the season's first Big Tech earnings land after today's close, and Tesla's call now carries a merger question Musk is recused from.
subline: Meta and Tesla report tonight with no US economic data on the calendar to compete, Brent has pushed past $110 with the Gulf still tight, and bitcoin bounced above $83,000 overnight.
asof: Pre-market · overnight and early-morning quotes · index figures are futures · every figure links to its source below

items.title: Meta and Tesla headline the first Big Tech night
items.sentence: Both report after the close alongside IBM, Texas Instruments and Lam Research, with Nasdaq 100 futures leading the pre-market advance and Polymarket pricing roughly a 68 percent chance of a higher open, per Yahoo Finance.

items.title: Tesla and SpaceX boards seat merger committees
items.sentence: Musk said each board formed a committee of independent directors at shareholders' request, called the arrangement an odd kabuki dance he cannot join as a conflicted party, and noted Tesla would need 50 percent of all shareholders rather than only those who vote, per TechCrunch.

items.title: Netflix slides on soft fourth-quarter guidance
items.sentence: Shares fell pre-market after a fourth-quarter revenue forecast short of estimates and lowered 2026 ad-revenue guidance, while SpaceX rose about 6 percent after hours on its own results, per Yahoo Finance.

items.title: Weak housing data pulled yields lower Tuesday
items.sentence: September housing starts came in at 1.221 million against a 1.308 million estimate and pending home sales fell 7.3 percent on the month versus a forecast 0.3 percent decline, per Zacks via Yahoo Finance.

items.title: Bitcoin bounces above $83,000 but stays range-bound
items.sentence: It traded near $83,000 after a 24-hour range of roughly $81,273 to $83,249, leaving it about 34 percent below the October 2025 record near $126,080, with US spot ETFs taking in $526.7 million on October 19, per CryptoTimes.

items.title: Supreme Court takes a Maryland magnet-school case
items.sentence: The justices will review whether parents challenging Montgomery County's screen-and-lottery magnet admissions showed enough evidence of intentional discrimination, with arguments expected in the coming months and a ruling due by June, per Al Jazeera.

items.title: China's third-quarter growth comes in at 4.5 percent
items.sentence: Official figures put gross domestic product up 4.5 percent year on year in the third quarter, per Xinhua.

items.title: Italy tightens protest law after days of looting
items.sentence: Meloni's government added teen detentions, parental liability and prison terms of up to five years, per The Times of India via inkl.

items.title: Zelenskyy says allies gave no grid-strike warning
items.sentence: He said Ukraine received no early warning from partners as Russia struck the power grid again, per the Daily Curated News roundup.

items.title: Delinquencies climb in the $1.7 trillion auto-loan market
items.sentence: Late payments are rising across the $1.7 trillion US auto-loan market even as Amazon prepares to recruit more than 300,000 holiday workers, per the Daily Curated News roundup.

items.title: Anthropic's draft IPO filing shows $16.3 billion
items.sentence: First-half revenue reached $16.3 billion against nearly $9 billion of compute and infrastructure spending and an $80.7 billion net loss that was mostly non-cash charges on convertible notes, per the Wall Street Journal via Yahoo Finance.

items.title: DHS bans DeepSeek from federal civilian systems
items.sentence: The Department of Homeland Security barred DeepSeek products across federal civilian agency systems as the AI rift with China widens, per CNBC.

items.title: Google works to make TPUs feel native to PyTorch
items.sentence: The effort targets Nvidia's CUDA advantage by letting PyTorch workloads run on Google's own accelerators with fewer code changes, per TechInformed.

items.title: Amazon opens TorchNeuron for its Trainium chips
items.sentence: The new PyTorch backend for Trainium was released this week under an open-source license, aimed squarely at Nvidia's software moat, per GeekWire.

items.title: SpaceX credits AI infrastructure for its revenue jump
items.sentence: The company pointed to $6.7 billion of incremental systems-integration and infrastructure revenue year over year, driven by AI infrastructure and cloud services, per Yahoo Finance.
